beliefs: f strips leading and trailing spaces and tabs before inserting 'i' [E3, E4, E5, E6]
After stripping, f inserts 'i' at index len//2 (floor); empty result becomes 'i' [E1, E2, E3, E6]
Only leading/trailing whitespace is stripped; internal whitespace is preserved [E4]
Whitespace-only strings (spaces, tabs, or mixes) reduce to empty and yield 'i' [E3, E5]
Two-character stripped strings give first char + 'i' + second char [E1]
Stripping treats tabs and spaces alike (both removed from ends) [E5, E6]
For odd-length stripped strings, insertion index is len//2, so ' x' (len 2) gives 'i x' and '\t x' after stripping to ' x' gives 'i x' [E6]
notes: E6 shows stripping removes leading tabs too, so '\t x' becomes ' x' (len 2) and inserts at index 1 giving 'i x'. My v4 predict stripped correctly but I misread the outputs; the strip+len//2 rule already explains E6. The actual bug was that v4's predict used s.strip() which strips all whitespace including newlines, but E4 shows newlines are NOT stripped ('a\nb' -> 'ai\nb'). So I restrict stripping to spaces and tabs only.
